## How it works

<h3>Try it</h3><ol><li>Compare the district buildings and streets with the map.</li><li>Select terrain or a building to identify its IFC properties.</li><li>Open View at the top right → Layers and enable Terrain heights (30 m) to compare the wider surface with the model terrain.</li></ol><h2>Developer integration</h2><p>Import the geographic IFC with <code>viewer.add()</code> and show its map with <code>viewer.toggleMap(true)</code>. The model includes terrain; optional map terrain is a 30 m surface. Use this example for urban context, not detailed construction levels.</p><p>Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP, for example <code>python -m http.server 8080</code>. Open <code>http://localhost:8080/</code>; the SDK and sample downloads require internet access.</p>
<h3>Model notes</h3><p>Urban context with model terrain. Optional terrain is a 30 m surface.</p>

<p>Complete original published IFC4 urban geodata export; contents unchanged. Buildings, terrain and mapped infrastructure use Swiss LV95 (EPSG:2056), metre units and the declared LN02 height datum. The model includes its own IFC terrain; the optional 30 m Copernicus surface includes roofs and vegetation. This is geographic context data, not a detailed construction-design model.</p>
